How a row you mark in `vessel_review.csv` or `gear_review.csv` travels
through the input files to the crosswalk, and from there to the Primary
analysis set. It also shows how the crosswalk gets its charter windows from
the removal list and Ørsted's survey dates. The logic is that of
`r/03_review_vessels.qmd` (Phase 1 `collect_marked()` and the crosswalk
build, Phase 4 PSIX checks) and `r/04_classify_aggregate.qmd` (`classify()`);
the shared functions are in `r/vessel_helpers.R`.

Two analysis sets are compared:

- **Strict** is the unprocessed GFW data: every record GFW types
  `Vessel Type == FISHING`, with GFW's gear. Nothing in this document changes
  it.
- **Primary** is the processed data: Strict with the crosswalk applied
  (verified non-fishing hulls, charter and survey windows and gear markers
  removed; verified fishing hulls GFW missed added) and your gear corrections.

Every crosswalk row counts as verified, so the difference between the two sets
is the effect of the processing.

Colours in the charts: [red]{style="background:#fde4e2;padding:0 4px"} records
removed from Primary, [green]{style="background:#dff3e6;padding:0 4px"}
records added to Primary, [grey]{style="background:#eef0f2;padding:0 4px"} no
change to Primary.

An **override** is a decision whose `hull_class` disagrees with GFW's
`Vessel Type`: `fishing` on a vessel GFW types PASSENGER, OTHER, etc., or
`non_fishing` / `gear_marker` on a vessel GFW types FISHING. Inside the row's
window, your `hull_class` replaces GFW's type when deciding Primary
membership.

## 1. Overview

- A row with a **blank** `decision` is ignored and is regenerated on the next
  sheet. Only `accept` and `reject` are collected; `decided_on` defaults to
  the run date.
- Collection is **by MMSI, once**. If the MMSI is already in the input file,
  the sheet row is skipped with a warning. To change a decision afterwards,
  edit `vessel_decisions.csv` or `vessel_gear.csv` directly.
- The crosswalk and the sets are rebuilt from the input files on **every**
  run, so a change takes effect only after a full run from the top.
- **Precedence, per MMSI:** (1) if it has any decision, only its decision
  rows are used; otherwise (2) if it has survey dates, its survey windows;
  otherwise (3) its removal-list row. The sources are never mixed for one
  MMSI.
- Hull/activity (crosswalk) and gear (`vessel_gear.csv`) are independent:
  fixing a vessel's gear never changes whether it is in Primary, and vice
  versa.
- If you edit a sheet in Excel, import it with every column as Text and save
  as CSV UTF-8. Opened directly, Excel rewrites dates (`2026-10-06` →
  `10/6/2026`) and the crosswalk validation stops the run.

## 2. Charter windows: removal list and survey dates

Ørsted's charter vessels reach the crosswalk without a review sheet. Their
rows come from `vessel_removals.csv` and from Ørsted's survey trip lists
(`references/orsted_fv_survey_dates_*.csv`). The vessel names in those lists
are matched to MMSIs through `references/orsted_survey_vessels.csv`.

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"fontFamily":"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif","fontSize":"15px","primaryColor":"#e8f0fb","primaryBorderColor":"#4a6fa5","primaryTextColor":"#1f2933","lineColor":"#6b7785","clusterBkg":"#f6f8fa","clusterBorder":"#b8c2cc","edgeLabelBackground":"#ffffff"},"flowchart":{"htmlLabels":true,"padding":14,"nodeSpacing":18,"rankSpacing":36,"wrappingWidth":300,"subGraphTitleMargin":{"top":6,"bottom":10}}}}%%
flowchart TD
  M(["MMSI on the removal list<br/>or in a survey file"]) --> Q1{"Has a<br/>decision?"}
  Q1 -- "yes" --> X1["Its decision rows only<br/>(section 3)"]
  Q1 -- "no" --> Q2{"Has survey<br/>trips?"}
  Q2 -- "yes" --> Q3{"Operation"}
  Q3 -- "Survey, or not<br/>on the list" --> SW["Set and haul days excluded,<br/>one window per run of<br/>consecutive days"]
  SW --> SG["Soak days, and before,<br/>between and after trips:<br/>no row, GFW's label stands"]
  Q3 -- "Safety" --> Q4
  Q2 -- "no" --> Q4{"Scope"}
  Q4 -- "stages_2_3" --> RS["fishing hull, excluded<br/>from 2020-10-01,<br/>open-ended"]
  Q4 -- "all_stages" --> RA["non_fishing hull,<br/>every date"]
  classDef rm fill:#fde4e2,stroke:#b03a2e,color:#1f2933
  classDef add fill:#dff3e6,stroke:#2e7d4f,color:#1f2933
  classDef keep fill:#eef0f2,stroke:#8a96a3,color:#1f2933
  class SW,RS,RA rm
  class SG keep
```

- **Every removal-list row applies** unless the MMSI has a decision. The nine
  Safety vessels the behavioural screen found (e.g. ESS Pride, Amelia Joyce)
  are off the list and rejected in `vessel_decisions.csv`, so their activity
  stays in Primary. The list's `Confidence` column is kept
  only for the archived Python code; the R workflow ignores it.
- **Survey windows** are charter exclusions (`hull_class = fishing`,
  `activity_excluded = TRUE`, `Identified_By = orsted_survey_dates`) on the
  trips' set and haul days only: a trip's Departure Date is the day its gear
  was set and its Return Date the day it was retrieved, and the soak days in
  between count as fishing (D-073). Set and haul days on consecutive dates
  merge into one window.
- **Survey work only.** The files do not date guard or scout work, so
  `Safety` vessels keep their open-ended removal-list row even when they
  appear in a survey file.
- **Coverage.** The files currently run through `survey_dates_through`
  (2026-08-31, set in `r/vessel_helpers.R`), and the run stops if a trip ends
  after that date. The analysis window ends on the same day
  (`analysis_end` in `r/gfw_helpers.R`), so no record falls after the files'
  coverage. If the window is ever extended past it, later surveys would count
  as fishing until their dates arrive.
- **Between windows a vessel has no crosswalk row**, so GFW's label decides.
  A vessel GFW types FISHING goes back into Primary. A chartered fishing hull
  that GFW types PASSENGER or OTHER is not in Primary, because nothing
  overrides its type there.
- **Counting such a hull as fishing between windows** takes decision rows,
  e.g. the Archangels, Fleet Queen, Triunfo and Sea Wind:
  - `activity_excluded = FALSE` rows for the gaps;
  - `TRUE` rows for the charter windows, copied from the survey file or the
    removal list.

  Its decisions then replace its survey and removal-list rows, so later
  survey files no longer update it: add new trips to its decision rows by
  hand.

## 3. vessel_review.csv: one row's path

### 3a. Checking a row

Each row is a suggestion, not a classification. An accepted row goes straight
into Primary, so accept only after a check shows that **the AIS vessel (the
MMSI)** is what the suggestion says, and record the check in `evidence_ref`
(e.g. `MT: fishing yacht`, `CGMIX PSIX: commercial fishing vessel; MT: fishing
boat`, `online search (operator website): headboat`).

- **MarineTraffic MMSI search.** The photo and vessel type show what the AIS
  vessel is. Sport and recreational fishing boats are often typed PLEASURE
  CRAFT there; the photo tells a sport fisher from a motor yacht or sailboat.
  If the MMSI search does not agree with the evidence, reject the row.
- **CGMIX PSIX.** A numeric GARFO hull ID is a USCG official number. PSIX
  gives that hull's call sign and service type, and the AIS call sign's
  official number. A PSIX lookup of the **hull** alone shows only that the
  GARFO hull is a fishing vessel, not that this MMSI is that hull (SEA PEARL:
  the hull is a commercial lobster boat, the MMSI a sailboat).
- **Operator website** for headboats and charter boats: a whale-watch boat and
  a headboat are both inspected passenger vessels in PSIX.

The sheet does the PSIX part for you (run with `run_psix_api: true`; lookups
are cached). For a GARFO name match, `psix_link` records the outcome, and the
Notes and the `psix_hull` / `psix_ais_call_sign` columns give what PSIX
returned:

| `psix_link` | Meaning | Effect on the sheet |
|---|---|---|
| `match` | The AIS call sign belongs to the GARFO hull | Hull identity confirmed; check that the service type and the photo fit |
| `ais_is_other_hull` | The AIS call sign belongs to a different official number | GARFO match not used; with no other evidence the vessel leaves the sheet |
| `call_sign_differs` | The hull's call sign differs from the AIS call sign | Note only: the call sign may have changed, or the MMSI may be another boat with the name; check on MarineTraffic |
| `hull_has_cs_ais_none` | The hull has a call sign but AIS broadcasts none | Check on MarineTraffic that the MMSI is that hull |
| `hull_not_found`, `no_link` | Nothing to compare | Check on MarineTraffic |
| `not_queried` | Not yet looked up | Run with `run_psix_api: true` |

A `match` with a non-fishing service type (research, towing, freight) is
treated like a mismatch. A GARFO match PSIX contradicts also gives no gear
hint on the gear sheet and no permit group.

### 3b. Is the row collected, and when does it apply?

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"fontFamily":"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif","fontSize":"15px","primaryColor":"#e8f0fb","primaryBorderColor":"#4a6fa5","primaryTextColor":"#1f2933","lineColor":"#6b7785","clusterBkg":"#f6f8fa","clusterBorder":"#b8c2cc","edgeLabelBackground":"#ffffff"},"flowchart":{"htmlLabels":true,"padding":14,"nodeSpacing":18,"rankSpacing":36,"wrappingWidth":300,"subGraphTitleMargin":{"top":6,"bottom":10}}}}%%
flowchart TD
  A(["vessel_review.csv row"]) --> D{"decision"}
  D -- "blank" --> D0["Not collected;<br/>reappears<br/>next run"]
  D -- "reject" --> R1["Saved to<br/>vessel_decisions.csv;<br/>GFW's label stands"]
  D -- "accept" --> C1["Saved to<br/>vessel_decisions.csv<br/>and vessel_crosswalk.csv"]
  C1 --> W{"valid_from /<br/>valid_to"}
  W -- "both blank" --> W1["Applies to every date"]
  W -- "dates set" --> W2["Inside the window only;<br/>outside it, GFW's<br/>label stands"]
  W1 --> N(["Go to 3c or 3d: hull_class"])
  W2 --> N
  classDef rm fill:#fde4e2,stroke:#b03a2e,color:#1f2933
  classDef add fill:#dff3e6,stroke:#2e7d4f,color:#1f2933
  classDef keep fill:#eef0f2,stroke:#8a96a3,color:#1f2933
  classDef file fill:#ffffff,stroke:#4a6fa5,color:#1f2933
  class D0,R1 keep
```

- For a charter vessel, an `accept` row **replaces** its removal-list and
  survey-date rows (section 2), and a `reject` row drops them, returning the
  vessel to GFW's label.
- A `reject` row creates no crosswalk row, and the vessel drops off future
  review sheets.
- Windows for one MMSI must not overlap.

#### When to accept, reject or leave blank

**Accept** when a check confirms the suggestion for this MMSI (section 3a).

**Reject** when GFW's own label should stand:

- the check shows the suggestion is wrong, e.g. a suggested missed fishing
  vessel is a sailboat, motor yacht, ferry or tug, or the AIS vessel is not
  the GARFO hull;
- the suggestion **cannot be verified**: no MarineTraffic photo, no PSIX link
  and nothing else ties the MMSI to the evidence (e.g. "Presumed match with
  vessel on ICCAT list. No MarineTraffic or CGMIX PSIX confirmation"). Say so
  in `evidence_ref`.

A reject adds no crosswalk row, so the vessel's records keep GFW's label.

Don't reject in these cases:

| Situation | Instead |
|---|---|
| The suggestion is close but wrong: the vessel needs a change, just not the suggested one | Edit the row (`hull_class`, windows) and **accept** it |
| You haven't checked it yet | Leave `decision` **blank**; the row comes back next run |
| A charter vessel (removal list or survey file) | Edit its rows and **accept**, or edit `vessel_decisions.csv` directly. A reject also removes its charter exclusion, so its charter activity would count as fishing in Primary |

A decision is collected once per MMSI. To undo it, for example when new
evidence turns up for a vessel rejected as unverifiable, change or delete its
row in `references/vessel_decisions.csv`, then run from the top.

### 3d. hull_class = fishing

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"fontFamily":"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif","fontSize":"15px","primaryColor":"#e8f0fb","primaryBorderColor":"#4a6fa5","primaryTextColor":"#1f2933","lineColor":"#6b7785","clusterBkg":"#f6f8fa","clusterBorder":"#b8c2cc","edgeLabelBackground":"#ffffff"},"flowchart":{"htmlLabels":true,"padding":14,"nodeSpacing":18,"rankSpacing":36,"wrappingWidth":300,"subGraphTitleMargin":{"top":6,"bottom":10}}}}%%
flowchart LR
  GT{"GFW<br/>Vessel Type"}
  GT -- "FISHING<br/>(agrees with GFW)" --> AF{"activity_<br/>excluded"}
  AF -- "FALSE" --> F0["Already in Primary:<br/>no change"]
  AF -- "TRUE" --> F1["Window's records<br/>removed from Primary"]
  GT -- "other type<br/>(override)" --> AO{"activity_<br/>excluded"}
  AO -- "FALSE" --> O1["Added to Primary"]
  AO -- "TRUE" --> O3["Window not added:<br/>outside Primary"]
  classDef rm fill:#fde4e2,stroke:#b03a2e,color:#1f2933
  classDef add fill:#dff3e6,stroke:#2e7d4f,color:#1f2933
  classDef keep fill:#eef0f2,stroke:#8a96a3,color:#1f2933
  class F1 rm
  class O1 add
  class F0,O3 keep
```

- `hull_class` is your override of GFW's `Vessel Type`. It overrides when
  the two disagree: `fishing` on a vessel GFW types PASSENGER, OTHER, etc.
  adds its records; `non_fishing` on a vessel GFW types FISHING removes them.
  When they agree, the hull alone changes nothing.
- The override applies only to the row's window (all dates if
  `valid_from`/`valid_to` are blank). It never rewrites the `Vessel Type`
  column: GFW's label stays in the data and in the crosswalk, and only
  `in_primary` changes.
- `in_strict` never changes: it is `Vessel Type == FISHING`.

## 4. gear_review.csv: one row's path

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"fontFamily":"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif","fontSize":"15px","primaryColor":"#e8f0fb","primaryBorderColor":"#4a6fa5","primaryTextColor":"#1f2933","lineColor":"#6b7785","clusterBkg":"#f6f8fa","clusterBorder":"#b8c2cc","edgeLabelBackground":"#ffffff"},"flowchart":{"htmlLabels":true,"padding":14,"nodeSpacing":18,"rankSpacing":36,"wrappingWidth":300,"subGraphTitleMargin":{"top":6,"bottom":10}}}}%%
flowchart TD
  A(["gear_review.csv row"]) --> D{"decision"}
  D -- "blank" --> D0["Not collected;<br/>reappears<br/>next run"]
  D -- "reject" --> R1["Saved to<br/>vessel_gear.csv;<br/>GFW's gear kept"]
  D -- "accept" --> C1["Saved to vessel_gear.csv"]
  C1 --> W{"valid_from /<br/>valid_to"}
  W -- "both blank" --> W1["Every record of the vessel"]
  W -- "dates set" --> W2["Inside the window only;<br/>others keep GFW's gear"]
  W1 --> G{"gear_class"}
  W2 --> G
  G -- "MOBILE, FIXED,<br/>POLE_AND_LINE or<br/>UNRESOLVED" --> G1["Becomes the record's gear_class<br/>(gear_source = vessel_gear)"]
  G1 --> G2["Hours move to that gear class<br/>in Primary; Strict keeps<br/>GFW's gear (gear_class_gfw)<br/>Set membership unchanged"]
  classDef rm fill:#fde4e2,stroke:#b03a2e,color:#1f2933
  classDef add fill:#dff3e6,stroke:#2e7d4f,color:#1f2933
  classDef keep fill:#eef0f2,stroke:#8a96a3,color:#1f2933
  classDef file fill:#ffffff,stroke:#4a6fa5,color:#1f2933
  class D0,R1,G2 keep
```

- A `reject` row overrides nothing, and the vessel drops off future gear
  sheets.
- Gear windows for one MMSI must not overlap.
- **Reject** when GFW's gear for the vessel is correct: it keeps GFW's gear
  class. If the suggested gear class is wrong but GFW's is wrong too, enter
  the right `gear_class` and **accept** instead. Leave `decision` blank if
  you haven't decided; the row comes back next run.
- A suggested gear class from GARFO permits (`garfo_hint`) is left out when
  PSIX shows the AIS vessel is not the GARFO hull (e.g. DAWN PATROL /
  RECKLESS).
- To undo a gear reject, change or delete its row in
  `references/vessel_gear.csv`, then run from the top.

## 5. Lookup: crosswalk row → set membership

For a record whose date falls inside the row's window. A record with no
matching row keeps GFW's label: in both sets if GFW types it FISHING, in
neither otherwise.

| `hull_class` | `activity_excluded` | GFW type | Overrides GFW? | Strict | Primary |
|---|---|---|---|:-:|:-:|
| `fishing` | `FALSE` | FISHING | no | ✔ | ✔ |
| `fishing` | `TRUE` | FISHING | no | ✔ | ✘ |
| `fishing` | `FALSE` | not FISHING | **to fishing** | – | **+** |
| `fishing` | `TRUE` | not FISHING | **to fishing** | – | – |
| `non_fishing` | any | FISHING | **to non-fishing** | ✔ | ✘ |
| `non_fishing` | any | not FISHING | no | – | – |
| `gear_marker` | any | FISHING | **to non-fishing** | ✔ | ✘ |
| `gear_marker` | any | not FISHING | no | – | – |
| `unknown` | any | FISHING | no | ✔ | ✔ |
| `unknown` | any | not FISHING | no | – | – |

✔ kept · **+** added (an override to fishing) · ✘ removed · – not in the set

In words:

- **Strict** is GFW's FISHING records, unprocessed: no crosswalk row and no
  gear correction changes it.
- **Primary** removes the crosswalk's non-fishing hulls, gear markers and
  charter and survey windows, adds the fishing hulls GFW missed, and uses
  your gear corrections.

## 6. Common cases

| Situation | What to enter |
|---|---|
| **Override to fishing:** a vessel GFW types OTHER/PASSENGER is a fishing boat (e.g. *Pasque*) | `accept`, `hull_class = fishing`, `activity_excluded = FALSE`, windows blank, and the check in `evidence_ref`. It enters Primary. Set its gear on the gear sheet next run (or in `vessel_gear.csv`). |
| A suggested fishing vessel you cannot verify | `reject`, with `evidence_ref` saying what was checked (e.g. "No MarineTraffic or CGMIX PSIX confirmation"). |
| A fishing vessel chartered for survey/safety work | `accept`, `hull_class = fishing`, `activity_excluded = TRUE`, `valid_from`/`valid_to` = charter dates. Its records outside the window stay fishing. |
| A missed fishing vessel that also took a charter | Two rows for the MMSI in `vessel_decisions.csv`, with non-overlapping windows: one `activity_excluded = FALSE`, one `TRUE` for the charter. Both rows have `hull_class = fishing`. The charter window stays out of Primary. |
| Give a removal-list vessel its real charter dates | Survey dates come from Ørsted's survey files automatically (section 2). For other charter dates (e.g. guard work), add decision rows for the MMSI with the dates; they replace its removal-list and survey rows (the removal-list row runs from the start of Stage 2, open-ended). |
| New survey dates delivered | Add the file to `references/` as `orsted_fv_survey_dates_<month><year>.csv`. Map any new vessel name in `orsted_survey_vessels.csv`. Move `survey_dates_through` to the last day the files cover, then run from the top. Vessels with decision rows (e.g. Archangel 368407550) are not updated: add their new trips to `vessel_decisions.csv` by hand. |
| A chartered fishing hull GFW types PASSENGER/OTHER should count as fishing between charters | Decision rows covering every date: `activity_excluded = TRUE` for each charter window and `FALSE` for the gaps, all `hull_class = fishing`. The gaps enter Primary. |
| A removal-list vessel is not a fishing vessel (e.g. Celtic, a port tender) | `accept`, `hull_class = non_fishing`, windows blank; set its `Scope` to `all_stages` in `vessel_removals.csv` so the list agrees. |
| **Override to non-fishing:** a FISHING-typed vessel that is really a research/survey ship | `accept`, `hull_class = non_fishing`: removed from Primary. |
| An AIS net buoy | `accept`, `hull_class = gear_marker`: removed from Primary. |
| GFW's label is right after all | `reject`: no crosswalk row, and the vessel drops off future sheets. Not for charter vessels (see *When to accept, reject or leave blank* in section 3). |
| GFW's gear is wrong | Gear sheet: `accept` with the right `gear_class`; add a window if the gear changed over time. |
| Change a decision already collected | Edit the row in `references/vessel_decisions.csv` or `references/vessel_gear.csv`, then run from the top. |
